product_guards: A same-host HTTP-to-HTTPS scheme proposal is not destination evidence. Require coherent, independently requested direct HTTPS HTML 200 observations at the exact same path/query/slash, with no fetch error, blocked host, redirect chain, non-self canonical, noindex or none directive. Conflicting duplicates refuse; missing canonical is allowed only when observations consistently show its absence. Refuse foreign hosts, credentials, fragments in proposals and explicit ports.

Require one literal sitemap in a known static directory, without a generator. Re-read unique literal HTML source bindings, current canonical/indexability and flat routing rules before writing. Refuse changed or ambiguous source/routing, wildcard or competing configurations, head scripts, templates, refresh and unverified language alternates on a moved entry.

Immediately before a single XML PUT, recheck each HTTPS destination with the existing public-target guard and bounded streamed GET: no credentials or redirects, typed 200, exact response URL, no history or Retry-After, HTML content type and no excluded X-Robots directive. Read at most 80000 bytes, decode UTF-8, require the same canonical and indexable literal head, and close the response on every path. Served body scripts are allowed for host-injected footers; source files remain script-free. One changed witness blocks the entire write.

Reuse validated XML nodes and byte offsets. Without collision, change only the exact loc text and preserve metadata; with an existing HTTPS destination, keep its complete entry and delete the obsolete HTTP entry. Preserve significant path case, slash, query, distinct fragment variants, comments, namespace URLs, extensions, unrelated duplicates and other entries. Reject DTD, indexes, malformed or ambiguous XML, unreadable SHA and oversized sources.

Individual and grouped deep endpoints share the guard, with zero provider calls and zero AI billing. Refused URLs are named when a verified subset exists. Empty guard plans prevent heuristic fallback, and free-form, cached and confirmed preview paths cannot bypass the evidence requirement. Generic mixed-content rewrites and their legacy collision contracts remain unchanged.

successful_live_cycle.preput_http_namespace: Only exact owned production-namespace destinations are mapped to the actual baseline preview host. The transport projects the response URL and removes only the verified exact Netlify noindex header; actual status, body, canonical, meta robots and stream are retained. This is a counterfactual fixture check, not a native preview passing the product guard.
successful_live_cycle.system_count_derivation: The auditor emits this family outside _score_issues. The controlled report repeats its sorted HTTP-loc set check from the actual served XML, rather than assuming _score_issues emits this key or inventing occurrence evidence.

independent_countercheck.checks: Re-read exact branch heads, closed draft PRs, successful builds, one-file Git comparisons, unique HTML bindings, current canonical/indexability, independently specified expected XML bytes, collision metadata, refused entries, served XML and five actual HTTP witnesses per preview. Compare healthy bodies with only the actual owned Netlify deploy-id normalized; compare the 404 body exactly. Re-prepare and rewrite the baseline with final code without targeting, models, writes or quota calls.
independent_countercheck.initial_checker_failure: The first read-only checker incorrectly required a Netlify footer on the default 404 body. It was corrected to compare the absent-footer 404 body exactly, preserving every source/HTTP/XML assertion. No product code or live result was altered for this checker correction.

initial_red.explanation: Repeated probes of unchecked scheme replacement, missing guards and collision metadata selection, not 71 independent defects.

first_implementation_run.explanation: An old positive fixture supplied no HTTPS page observations. Add a real-shaped direct HTML 200 witness, preserving every original rewrite/evidence assertion.

first_endpoint_run.explanation: The new root-URL expectation used a prefix replacement and accidentally changed its negative control too. Correct the expected complete loc match; product output already preserved the control.

first_full_suite.explanation: Enrich the old positive branch-selection fixture with independent healthy HTTPS observations, retain its original named-rewriter assertion through the existing wrapper, and rerun the full suite after adding the distinct-fragment guard.

limitations: Only an owned static HTML repository with a unique literal XML sitemap, unique script-free HTML sources and simple routing is rebuilt. Generated, dynamic, multiple/ambiguous sitemaps, nonliteral heads, language annotations on moved entries, large/non-UTF8 served documents and explicit URL ports are conservatively refused. Project site_name must identify the actual host for this existing proposal API; a friendly label alone does not establish ownership. This is not coverage of every correctable stack or every occurrence.

Two negative HTTP entries deliberately remain: their HTTPS destinations are noindex or 404. Correcting all three selected positives does not establish resolution of the whole family. Broken/protected/redirecting/currently changed destinations and body/head script distinctions are also tested synthetically, not recreated on every remote stack.

Native previews retain noindex headers and canonical-host context, and raw sitemap seeds remain zero. Raw family counts 0 to 0 prove no repair. Counterfactual host/header projection and actual served XML yield 5 to 2, independently checked against sources and HTTP. No production indexation or runtime JavaScript DOM execution is proven.

The public-target validator is reused; this phase is not a full SSRF/DNS-rebinding audit. Git reads, sitemap SHA, streamed HTTP probes and a future deployment are not an atomic transaction. Concurrent or later source/server changes remain possible. Body-script allowance is for served HTML inspection only, not inferred source generation.

No agent deployment, client onboarding, fresh real Claude integration, production recovery replay, scheduler/payment acceptance, capacity test or fresh PostgreSQL run is included. SQLite retains 42 skipped tests. Ten claimed families still have no exact named record, and record references themselves are not successful repairs. No all-green catalog or client-readiness certification is claimed.
